thread:
support-ops: FYI we just got an escalation from ACME. Their p99 on /v1/generate jumped from ~1.2s to ~4.5s around 2026-03-14T22:10Z. They say our dashboard shows the spike but their raw service histograms look smaller. Screenshot attached.

maria: adding details — customer on Dedicated eu-west-1, model=gpt-medium-4q, tenant id T-ACME-9. Client retries also increased during window.

aj: can you paste the dashboard link + the raw histogram query? my gut says rollup vs raw aggregation mismatch.

support-ops: dashboard: https://console.redwood/d/abcd/p95-latency?orgId=1&var-tenant=T-ACME-9
raw per-instance histogram (from metrics store):
```
# ClickHouse-ish
SELECT quantile(0.99)(lat_ms) AS p99
FROM requests
WHERE tenant_id = 'T-ACME-9' AND api_path = '/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN toDateTime('2026-03-14 21:50:00') AND toDateTime('2026-03-14 22:20:00')
```

cheng: looking — dashboard panel is using the aggregated rollup series: `histogram_rollup:requests:latency:1m` which we compress from per-instance histograms. Rollup uses boundary-normalization that can move mass across le buckets when instances have different bucket sets. That can inflate high-quantiles in some windows.

linda: this smells like the bucket-alignment change we shipped for high-cardinality tenants (the one that coarsens boundaries when seq_len>1024). If an instance reports slightly shifted bucket edges the rollup normalizes to the union of edges and that can bias quantile() upwards.

maria: repro steps (from support):
```
# quick repro we ran in staging
ab -n 5000 -c 50 -H "X-Test-Spike: true" -p payload.json https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate
# payload uses sequence_length ~ 800, batch size 1
```
We also saw KV cache miss rate jump 8x at t+30s in the tenant logs.

aj: actionable plan:
- short term: increase dedicated pool for T-ACME-9 + enable extra burst capacity for 15m to absorb retries (ops escalation done).
- short term: flip dashboard panel to use raw per-instance quantiles (not rollup) so support/customer sees the true p99.
- medium: add a guard in the rollup code to avoid union-normalization for incompatible bucket sets (or fall back to per-instance p99 for important tenants).
- medium: patch collector to keep a canonical bucket mapping for quantile rollups.

support-ops: ops already bumped pool by +20% and enabled tenant burst at 22:18Z — can confirm latency dropped back to ~1.4s within 6m, per instance traces. Customer still unhappy with dashboard mismatch and wants explanation.

cheng: I'll dig into the rollup normalization code, I can reproduce with two simulated instances that send shifted bucket boundaries. Quick test: if instance A has edges [0.1,0.5,1,2] and B has [0.2,0.6,1.2,2.4], the union mapping causes more weight in the high bucket when we expand counts to union edges -> quantile worsens.

linda: assigning myself to a short-term fix: update the p99 panel to a templated query that can switch between `histogram_rollup` and `per_instance_histogram` per tenant. I'll push a dashboard patch and a note in the incident thread. ETA 1h.

aj: meanwhile @cheng please prepare a minimal repro and a unit test for the rollup normalization behavior. If we can't quickly find a safe canonicalization, we'll add a protection that refuses to rollup when bucket sets diverge > 10% edge mismatch.

sre-bot: Incident stub created — INC-2026-0314-TACME-LATENCY. Owners: ops (maria), eng-sre (cheng), metrics (aj), observability (linda).

maria: final note — customer reported a billing metric spike (retries -> more tokens) so we should include cost/regression brief in the postmortem. Support ticket #S-9444.

aj: summary/action items:
- linda: update dashboard -> use per-instance p99 for now (ETA 1h).
- cheng: reproduce & PR for rollup normalization unit tests (ETA EOD).
- maria/ops: validate dedicated bump and tenant burst logs, confirm no further retries (in progress).
- support-ops: communicate to customer that we mitigated the load and root cause is metrics rollup mismatch, not model slowdown (draft message ready).

support-ops: customer reply: thanks for the quick assist, they will keep monitoring and asked for a postmortem. :thumbsup:

aj: ping if anything else pops up. I'll file the postmortem template and link here. :eyes:
